title: Walkie-talkies and other devices explode across Lebanon a day after the pager blasts
body:
On 18 September 2024, a day after about 4,000 Hezbollah pagers exploded, a second wave of explosions hit devices across Lebanon. Al Jazeera reported that blasts affected walkie-talkie radios, mobile phones, laptops and solar power cells, mostly communication systems. Blasts were reported in Beirut's southern suburbs and in the southern city of Tyre, and a car reportedly exploded during a funeral in southern Lebanon.

Al Jazeera put the toll at between 14 and 20 killed and 450 injured in its early reporting, without naming a source for the figures. The walkie-talkies appeared to be IC-V82 radios made by the Japanese company ICOM, which said it had stopped producing them about ten years earlier. The previous day's pager explosions had killed 12 people and injured nearly 3,000, according to the same report. Lebanese Health Minister Firass Abiad said that those with serious injuries were severely affected.

The cause was unclear at the time. Hezbollah and the Lebanese government blamed Israel, which had not commented. Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant said the army would shift forces and resources from the war in Gaza to the north. Hezbollah said it fired rockets at Israeli artillery positions, which Reuters described as its first strike on Israel since the pager attacks. Analyst Elijah Magnier said Israel aimed to create confusion within Hezbollah and Lebanese society.
